It is written for the model that reads this object next, which is the model writing it, with nothing else in its context; use whatever form carries the most.", "text": "STORY STATE (prose fiction, past tense, close 3rd person on Marit).
SETTING: Vardnes, Norwegian coastal village, pop. 212 (last census). Lighthouse plus keeper's cottage on the point. Ferry Kittiwake passes the point at 16:40 every Tue and Fri.
MARIT SOLVANG, 47. Lives alone near the shore. Father Eirik. Grandmother Signe kept the village tide table for 40 years. Brother Tomas works at the Bergen fish plant and phones Sundays.
ANDERS HOLM: lighthouse keeper. Left Vardnes on 2 March, reason unknown. His cottage key hangs on a nail behind Marit's door.
CORE MYSTERY: the tides are arriving early. Holm's logbook records the drift beginning last July: +4 min, then +9, then +22.
SO FAR: Today the tide came in an hour early. At 13:09, 51 minutes before the table's 14:00, Marit's mussel bucket on the flat rock went under. Water reached her shed doorstep, so she moved the outboard motor up to the loft. Three gulls sat on the breakwater; a fourth lay dead on the shingle. She took Holm's key and logbook and walked to the cottage before dark. The cottage barometer read 1003 and had not moved in a week.
NEW EVENT: At the cottage table she opened the logbook to its last page. Holm's final entry was dated 1 March: '+51 min. Signe's numbers were right. Tell no one until the 40th.' Below it was a column of future dates and times in his hand. Today's line read '13:09'. The next line read 'Fri 12:31'. Friday is the ferry day.
OPEN THREADS: Who or what are 'Signe's numbers'? What is 'the 40th'? Where did Holm go? Will Friday's early tide affect the Kittiwake? Will Marit tell Tomas on Sunday? Is the dead gull or the stuck barometer significant?"}
